scope: Actual all-layer port-component identification and physically adjacent LONG_EDGE merge only
facts: All19 source/support spans SHA/base64 exact to fixed worker. Stream flatten layer->nodes->ports preserves encounter order; initialize only gathered ports toid-1; do not invent initialization of other reachable objects.

DFS assigns port id on entering. External neighbors incoming sources then outgoing targets; recurse full each before next; LONG_EDGE then other owned ports. Explicit iterator-frame stack mapping preserves recursive continuation and removes Python depth cap, not source semantics.

No label dummies: allowMerge uses firstport component-id equality even when both endpoint markers differ. sameSource/Target require current marker nonnull and exact native identity. Empty invalid port arrays not silently repaired.
Label dummy cases separately gate source sides by BEFORE and target sides by notBEFORE, with no-label exemptions; then allow via sameSource eligible or sameTarget eligible.

Only adjacent physical LONG_EDGE nodes within same layer considered. Successful removal retains previous as current and rechecks next neighbor using updated marker state. NORMAL/LABEL/NS break adjacency.
Move each source port incoming/outgoing by taking current first repeatedly and real detach+append setters into retained first WEST/EAST ports; preserve identities and adjacency order.
Remove marker using null setter only if keep flagfalse. Layer array splice does NOT null removed node.layer or destroy empty ports. This intentionally differs from generic node deletion.
Existing property defaults false/null and native identity graph helpers reused; only ordered collection/iterator mapping, no Guava/GWT stream runtime copy.
limitations: Not full hyperedge graph admission, default scheduler activation, crossing counters, long-edge or label-dummy creation, routing or complete layered implementation.
